title: Peripheral sensitization
objective: Explain how inflammation lowers nociceptor thresholds at the ending.

steps.title: Turning up the ending
steps.body: Injured or inflamed tissue releases a mix of mediators (an 'inflammatory soup': protons, bradykinin, prostaglandins, cytokines). These act on the [[nociceptor]] ending to **lower its [[threshold]]** — **[[peripheral sensitization]]**. Stimuli that were once sub-threshold now fire the neuron.

steps.prompt: What is the direct effect of peripheral sensitization on a nociceptor?
options: Its firing threshold drops, so weaker stimuli now excite it
Its axon suddenly conducts much faster all the way up to the cord
It fires as before, but the dorsal horn amplifies the signal instead
Its threshold rises, so stronger stimuli are now needed to excite it
steps.explanation: Inflammatory mediators modify channels at the ending, lowering threshold. The neuron now fires to stimuli it used to ignore — the cell type and conduction speed don't change.

variants.setup: Inflammatory mediators bathe a nociceptor ending.
options: It stays the same; only the cord's gain changes
variants.reveal: Peripheral sensitization lowers the threshold, so weaker stimuli now fire it.

steps.setup: Sunburned skin hurts when warm water hits it, though the same water felt fine before.
options: Peripheral sensitization has lowered the heat threshold of nociceptors
Only the dorsal horn changed; the endings in the skin are normal
The burned skin now conducts heat faster to the nerve endings
Heat-sensing nociceptors have multiplied in number in the burned skin
steps.reveal: Inflammation from the burn sensitizes the endings (e.g. via TRPV1 modulation), so merely warm water now crosses the lowered threshold — the classic everyday example.

variants.prompt: Warm water hurting sunburned skin is explained by…
options: A central change only, with normal endings in the skin
More heat-sensing nociceptors having grown in the burned skin
variants.explanation: Inflammation lowers the heat threshold, so warm now reads as painful.
